name: Mojisola Oluwatunbi
feedback: D1 is a complete, evidence-led catalogue. You captured all ten findings with the correct OWASP class, a correct CWE, and a quoted source line or capture timestamp for each: SQLi at login.php 64-67 with the 02:15:31 302, unsalted MD5 at line 66 (CWE-916/759), alg:none at 48-50 tied to Token 2, the hard-coded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 at line 30 (CWE-798), missing expiry at 76-81 (CWE-613), stored XSS at 02:18:47 with the beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443, XXE from 04-import-xxe.xml, path traversal at 02:24:02 returning root:x:0:0, the open redirect at 02:21:13, and the insecure cookie at line 86. Best of all, you nailed the decoy: you named the tempting HS256 branch and proved it safe at the mechanism level, hash_equals is constant-time against a properly computed HMAC, and you correctly located the real risk in alg:none and the weak secret rather than calling the whole JWT block broken. That is exactly right and it earns full marks. D2 is strong on payloads, CVSS, and impact, but the chain itself is the soft spot. You compressed the intrusion into four hops and did not reconcile the recon at 02:14:08, the failed guess at 02:14:55, the stored XSS at 02:18:47, and the open redirect at 02:21:13 into the chain narrative, so the hop-by-hop ordering is thinner than the evidence allows. Your SQLi vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N at 9.4, which is defensible on your shared-service reasoning, but the cleaner call at the injection step is S:U for roughly 9.1, with the scope change S:C reserved for the forged super_admin token reaching /api/v1/internal, which you did capture well as the senior insight. Your impact section is excellent: 312 customers, balances from about 6,400 to 950,000 naira, an aggregate in the tens of millions, the BoltCash six-week launch tie, and a stated assumption that the 20 sample rows are representative. D3 is the standout deliverable. The executive summary is genuinely jargon-free and lands on the customers-and-naira headline, the threat model reads the attacker correctly as a deliberate human in under seventeen minutes, every finding is tied to an evidence line, the decoy is restated correctly, the earliest-break fix is clear (fix step one and the chain collapses), and crucially your remediation table is ordered by effort-to-risk, not by raw CVSS, with the four-to-eight-hour parameterised-query fix ranked first for the most risk removed per hour. Both detection stopgaps are concrete with an exact field and a false-positive rate: the WAF regex keyed on the username and password POST parameters, and the SIEM rule keyed on the decoded JWT header alg field, each with a justified near-zero FP rate. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice and anchors to your own reconstructed timeline, and you carry ISC2 Canon II and Canon I as load-bearing on the journalist refusal and the NDPC notification. The one clear gap is that you reference the NDPA 2023 breach duty without the section number; name section 40 for the 72-hour NDPC notification and section 41 for notifying the 312 data subjects on high risk, and that row is complete. No figure here was invented; every number traces to the pack, so there is no fabrication penalty. The single most important fix: rebuild the D2 exploit chain as the full ordered sequence of hops from recon through exfil, each reconciled to its capture timestamp, and correct the SQLi scope to S:U at the injection step.
